partners.hero.title: Money only moves as far as *the rails beneath it.*
partners.hero.lead: A money app is only as trustworthy as the licence and the banks behind it. tazdan is building on licensed rails, one market at a time — and this page shows exactly where each relationship stands.
partners.hero.note: Pre-launch. Nothing on this page is a licence or an approval — it’s an honest account of where we are.
partners.rail.label: Stages of our partner pipeline
partners.pains.title: Without the right rails, *money gets stuck.*
partners.pains.lead: Most of what goes wrong with money in Libya isn’t the app on your phone. It’s what sits underneath it.
partners.pains.1.pain: Your money leaves one bank and sits in limbo for days before it reaches another — and nobody can tell you where it is.
partners.pains.1.fix: Direct relationships with Libyan banks are how deposits and payouts can land in your own account, with a reference you can follow.
partners.pains.2.pain: Your card is declined the moment you pay for something abroad — a booking, a course, a subscription you actually need.
partners.pains.2.fix: A card-issuing programme on a global network is how a card funded from your own balance could work wherever that network is accepted.
partners.pains.3.pain: There’s no regulated way to hold digital dollars — just a stranger, an envelope of cash and a promise.
partners.pains.3.fix: Regulated on-ramp and liquidity partners are what make buying USDT an ordinary, accountable transaction, where it’s permitted.
partners.pains.4.pain: Money apps appear, take deposits and vanish — because nobody ever licensed them.
partners.pains.4.fix: That’s why we’re pursuing licensing first: an app you can hold to account, with a supervisor behind it.
partners.status.title: Every relationship, *exactly as it is.*
partners.status.lead: Three stages, from the licence everything rests on to the partners we’re still evaluating. No logos, no borrowed credibility — just the status, and what has to happen next.
partners.stage.licensing.name: Licensing
partners.stage.licensing.desc: The permission to operate — the ground everything else is built on.
partners.stage.banking.name: Banking
partners.stage.banking.desc: Local rails, so dinars move between tazdan and your own bank.
partners.stage.pipeline.name: Pipeline
partners.stage.pipeline.desc: Global partners we’re evaluating for cards, top-ups and exchange. Most will need our licensing in place first.
partners.entry.meansLabel: What it would mean for you
partners.entry.cbl.name: Central Bank of Libya
partners.entry.cbl.role: Licensing. Our application is in preparation.
partners.entry.cbl.means: An independent supervisor over how your money is held, moved and reported — and the standing to connect properly with Libyan banks.
partners.entry.cbl.next: Complete our licensing application, file it, and work through the central bank’s review.
partners.entry.banks.name: Libyan banks
partners.entry.banks.role: Libyan commercial banks for dinar deposits, settlement and payouts to local accounts.
partners.entry.banks.means: Top up from your own bank account and withdraw back to it in dinars, with transfers matched by reference instead of chased by phone.
partners.entry.banks.next: Conversations are open. Next: agree terms, open settlement accounts and connect deposits and payouts.
partners.entry.visa.role: A card-issuing programme on the Visa network.
partners.entry.visa.means: Virtual and physical cards funded from your tazdan balance, for paying online and abroad wherever Visa is accepted. Cards are designed into the app and stay off until then.
partners.entry.visa.next: Line up a licensed issuer to run the programme, then complete Visa’s programme review.
partners.entry.banxa.role: A fiat on- and off-ramp: card and bank top-ups into digital assets, and back.
partners.entry.banxa.means: Top up by card or bank transfer and buy digital dollars like USDT in one step — or cash out the other way — where it’s permitted.
partners.entry.banxa.next: Finish our evaluation, complete their partner onboarding and confirm where the service is permitted for our customers.
partners.entry.cryptocom.means: Deep liquidity from an established exchange behind every buy and sell in the app, so your orders are executed against a real market.
partners.entry.cryptocom.next: Finish our evaluation, complete institutional onboarding and connect order execution to the app.
partners.footnote.trademarks: Names are trademarks of their owners and are shown as plain text, not logos. Listing a company here does not, by itself, mean an agreement is in place or that it endorses tazdan.
partners.footnote.status: Statuses reflect where things stood on the review date above and will change as work moves on. Nothing on this page is a licence, an approval or an offer of regulated services.
partners.unlock.eyebrow: Built, and waiting for its rails
partners.unlock.title: The app is built. *The rails come next.*
partners.unlock.lead: Some of this already works in the app; some is built and switched off. Partners are what take each one the rest of the way.
partners.unlock.banks.pain: “I made the transfer on Sunday. It’s Thursday, and I still can’t see it.”
partners.unlock.banks.title: Bank transfers today. *Direct bank links next.*
partners.unlock.banks.body: The app already takes top-ups by bank transfer to a tazdan account, and withdrawals to your own bank — each one checked and confirmed by our team. Links with Libyan banks are how that becomes automatic matching and faster payouts.
partners.unlock.banks.alt: Topping up by bank transfer in the tazdan app
partners.unlock.remit.pain: Money from family abroad goes through a middleman, takes a week, and arrives short.
partners.unlock.remit.title: Twelve corridors, *tested end to end.*
partners.unlock.remit.body: Locked quotes, compliance checks, tracking and refunds all run today on sandbox rails. A corridor goes live only when a licensed payout partner serves it — not a day before.
partners.unlock.remit.alt: Tracking a transfer abroad in the tazdan app
partners.unlock.remit.link: Licensed payout operator? Talk to us
partners.unlock.cards.pain: “Card declined.” At the checkout, on the booking site, on the course you were about to start.
partners.unlock.cards.title: A card, *designed in.*
partners.unlock.cards.body: Virtual and physical cards are designed into the app, funded straight from your balance. They stay switched off until a licensed card-issuing programme is in place.
partners.unlock.cards.alt: The cards screen in the tazdan app
partners.unlock.dollars.pain: Buying dollars means meeting a stranger with cash and hoping the other half of the deal arrives.
partners.unlock.dollars.title: Buy USDT *in the open.*
partners.unlock.dollars.body: Buy and sell USDT at live prices, with every step on the ledger and nothing handed over on a street corner. On-ramp and liquidity partners are how card top-ups and deeper markets could follow, where permitted.
partners.unlock.dollars.alt: Buying USDT in the tazdan app
partners.criteria.title: One bar, *for every partner.*
partners.criteria.lead: Global name or local bank, a partner only gets near your money if it clears all six.
partners.criteria.licensed.title: Licensed where they operate
partners.criteria.licensed.body: Authorised by the regulator in every market they serve. No licence, no integration.
partners.criteria.local.title: Present where it matters
partners.criteria.local.body: Real people and real accounts in Libya, or in the corridor they serve — not a mailbox and a website.
partners.criteria.safeguarding.title: Customer money kept apart
partners.criteria.safeguarding.body: Customer funds held separately from the partner’s own, so your money is never part of someone else’s balance sheet.
partners.criteria.aml.title: Sanctions and AML to our standard
partners.criteria.aml.body: Screening and anti-money-laundering controls at least as strict as the ones we run ourselves.
partners.criteria.arabic.title: Support in Arabic
partners.criteria.arabic.body: When something goes wrong with your money, you shouldn’t need a translator to fix it.
partners.criteria.reconcile.title: Built to reconcile
partners.criteria.reconcile.body: Idempotent requests, signed callbacks and daily statements — so a retry never pays twice and every dinar is accounted for.
partners.forPartners.title: Building rails into Libya? *Let’s talk.*
partners.forPartners.lead: We work with banks, payment providers, card issuers, remittance operators and liquidity venues that want to reach Libya properly. Here is what you’d be plugging into.
partners.forPartners.who.banks.title: Banks
partners.forPartners.who.banks.body: Dinar accounts, deposits, settlement and payouts.
partners.forPartners.who.psps.title: Payment providers
partners.forPartners.who.issuers.title: Card issuers
partners.forPartners.who.liquidity.title: Liquidity venues
partners.forPartners.bring.app.title: An Arabic-first app
partners.forPartners.bring.app.body: Designed in Arabic from the first screen, available in ten languages, coming to iPhone and Android.
partners.forPartners.bring.kyc.title: Verified customers
partners.forPartners.bring.kyc.body: Identity checks with document review, verification levels and live limits before money moves — and KYB for businesses.
partners.forPartners.bring.ledger.title: A ledger that always balances
partners.forPartners.bring.ledger.body: Double-entry, enforced by the database at commit. Customer, settlement and corporate money sit in separate fund classes and reconcile against partner statements.
partners.forPartners.bring.cockpit.title: Control Cockpit
partners.forPartners.bring.cockpit.body: Operations tooling with 12 staff roles and 49 permissions, maker-checker approvals, kill switches and an audit trail on every action.
partners.forPartners.bring.compliance.bo: Sanctions screening, a 17-rule risk engine and case management on transfers and withdrawals.
partners.forPartners.bring.api.title: Ready for your API
partners.forPartners.bring.api.body: Adapter interfaces for payouts, cards, on-ramps and banks, with idempotency keys, signed webhooks and sandbox test suites. Your adapter replaces a sandbox rail — nothing else changes.
partners.cta.title: Be there when *the rails go live.*
